experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling local cheeses, exotic meats, fresh juices, and traditional Mexican street food. Ideal for Day 1 arrival since it's open late and located centrally near recommended hotels in Centro Histórico. A perfect low-key introduction after a late flight.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived, now a museum showcasing her personal belongings, artwork, and life story. Book tickets in advance to avoid queues. Stay in Coyoacán neighborhood to walk here easily and maximize time on arrival days.

experiences.name: Tacos and Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Spend an evening hopping between taquerías and mezcalerías in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood. Try al pastor tacos at El Huequito and sip artisanal mezcal at local bars. This neighborhood is walkable and vibrant, making it ideal for travelers staying in Roma or Condesa.

experiences.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning bus from Terminal Norte to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, climbing the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon. Arrive by 9am to beat crowds and heat. Budget-friendly and one of the most awe-inspiring cultural experiences in all of Mexico. Return by early afternoon.
experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (day trip from Mexico City)

experiences.name: Cooking Class in Condesa
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Mexican cooking class in the leafy Condesa neighborhood, learning to make mole, tamales, and salsas from scratch using local market ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit to Mercado Medellín. Perfect mid-trip activity to deepen food knowledge and culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival. Take the Metro Line 1 (pink) from Aeropuerto station to Centro Histórico – costs only $5 MXN (~$0.25 USD). Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely walk to the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry). Stroll along the pedestrian street Madero, soaking in the colonial architecture and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the lit-up Zócalo as the sun sets – the square is magical at dusk. Explore the surrounding streets of Centro Histórico and get oriented with your neighborhood.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap meal at a street taco stand near the airport or around the Zócalo upon arrival. Look for tacos de canasta (basket tacos) for around $10–15 MXN each (~$0.50–0.75 USD).
meals.dinner: Head to Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén or a nearby fondas (family-run eateries) for a comida corrida (set meal) – soup, main dish, drink, and dessert for around $80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD). Try pozole or enchiladas.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your luggage light and secure on the Metro. Exchange some cash at the airport or use a fee-free ATM (avoid Banamex exchange counters). The Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to get around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the iconic Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~$85 MXN / ~$4 USD), the ancient Aztec temple unearthed in the heart of Centro Histórico. The attached museum is included in the ticket and is world-class. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ruins and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior is free; murals inside ~$80 MXN) to admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Then head to Alameda Central Park – a beautiful public park just steps away – and relax among locals. Visit the nearby Museo Mural Diego Rivera (free on Sundays, ~$45 MXN other days) to see Rivera's famous 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Park' mural.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bohemian neighborhood of Barrio Chino (Mexico City's small Chinatown) on Calle Dolores, just off Alameda. Then stroll back toward the Zócalo for a nighttime view of the illuminated cathedral.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your hotel if breakfast is included, or visit a nearby panadería (bakery) for pan dulce and café de olla for under $40 MXN (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Try a torta (Mexican sandwich) from a street vendor near Bellas Artes for $50–70 MXN (~$2.50–3.50 USD). Look for tortas de milanesa or tortas ahogadas.
meals.dinner: Visit Mercado de San Juan (Calle Ernesto Pugibet) for fresh, affordable local food stalls. Try quesadillas with huitlacoche (corn fungus) or tlayudas for around $60–100 MXN (~$3–5 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect. Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover several kilometers today. Carry a reusable water bottle; tap water is not drinkable, but purified water stations are cheap (~$5 MXN per refill).

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán neighborhood (Line 3 to Viveros station). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo – the 'Blue House' (Casa Azul). Book tickets online in advance (~$270 MXN / ~$13 USD) as they sell out fast. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the life and art of Frida Kahlo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Museo León Trotsky (entry ~$50 MXN / ~$2.50 USD), the former home and final resting place of the Russian revolutionary. Then explore the charming Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo in Coyoacán's town center – a vibrant, tree-lined square full of street vendors, artisans, and locals.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Coyoacán for the evening. Browse the weekend-style artisan market stalls around the plaza. Head back to Centro Histórico via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local market breakfast spot in Centro before heading out – try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros for $60–90 MXN (~$3–4.50 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of Coyoacán's market fondas inside Mercado de Coyoacán. Try enfrijoladas or mole dishes for $80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD). The market is lively and authentic.
meals.dinner: Pick up antojitos (street snacks) from vendors around Jardín Centenario – tostadas, tlacoyos, or memelas for $20–40 MXN each (~$1–2 USD). A filling dinner for under $100 MXN total.

day_by_day.notes: Metro fare is $5 MXN per ride (~$0.25 USD) – incredibly affordable. Coyoacán is one of the safest and most walkable neighborhoods in CDMX. Pre-book Frida Kahlo museum tickets online at museofridakahlo.org.mx to avoid disappointment.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city with massive pyramids (~50 km from the city center). Catch an early bus from Terminal del Norte (Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte station). Round-trip bus fare is ~$100–130 MXN (~$5–6.50 USD). Site entry is ~$90 MXN (~$4.50 USD). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon for breathtaking views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl at Teotihuacán. Browse local artisan stalls near the entrance for affordable obsidian souvenirs. Head back to Mexico City by mid-afternoon (buses run frequently).
day_by_day.evening: Rest briefly at the hotel, then head to the lively Plaza Garibaldi (10-minute walk from the Zócalo) to hear mariachi bands perform – it's free to listen from the plaza. The atmosphere is festive and quintessentially Mexican.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing – grab tamales and atole from a street vendor near the Metro station for ~$40–60 MXN (~$2–3 USD). Tamales are a traditional Mexican breakfast.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the simple comedores (small eateries) near the Teotihuacán site entrance. A basic set meal costs ~$100–150 MXN (~$5–7.50 USD). Alternatively, pack snacks from a OXXO convenience store to save money.
meals.dinner: Near Plaza Garibaldi, try birria (slow-cooked goat or beef stew) from a local taquería for ~$80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD). The area has many affordable options.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Teotihuacán early (it opens at 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and midday heat. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water – the site is exposed and can get warm even in March. Wear sturdy shoes for climbing the pyramids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park – one of the greatest museums in the world (entry ~$85 MXN / ~$4 USD, free on Sundays). Take Metro Line 1 to Chapultepec station. Spend 2–3 hours marveling at Aztec, Maya, and other Mesoamerican artifacts, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) – entry to the park is free. Rent a rowboat on the lake (~$100 MXN / ~$5 USD for 30 minutes) or simply relax on the grass with locals. Walk up to Castillo de Chapultepec (entry ~$85 MXN / ~$4 USD) for panoramic views of the city and to see the National History Museum inside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Condesa or Roma Norte neighborhoods (walkable from Chapultepec) for a final evening stroll. Browse the tree-lined streets, street art, and charming architecture. End the trip with a celebratory mezcal or craft beer at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local mercado in Centro Histórico before heading out – try a hearty breakfast of eggs, beans, and tortillas at a market comedor for $60–80 MXN (~$3–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat near Chapultepec at one of the many taco stands or food trucks along Avenida Presidente Masaryk or inside the park. Budget $80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD) for tacos al pastor or tacos de suadero.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night at a casual restaurant in Colonia Roma – try El Turix for cochinita pibil tacos (~$30–40 MXN each) or visit Mercado Roma (a gourmet food market) for a variety of affordable bites ranging from $50–150 MXN (~$2.50–7.50 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología alone is worth at least half a day – it's enormous. If time is short, prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls. Chapultepec Park is a beloved local hangout and gives you an authentic glimpse of everyday CDMX life. Keep small bills handy for street food vendors.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approx. 45–60 min by taxi or Uber). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the Catedral Metropolitana exterior and stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the colonial architecture. Stop by Palacio Nacional to admire Diego Rivera's famous murals in the courtyard — entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets of Centro Histórico as they come alive at dusk. Walk along Madero Street (pedestrian zone) and enjoy the atmosphere. Head to a rooftop bar for a welcome mezcal or michelada with views of the historic skyline.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and authentic bite at Mercado de San Juan or a nearby taquería — try tacos de canasta or tlayudas for a true local introduction (budget ~150–200 MXN).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de Tacuba, a historic and beloved restaurant in Centro Histórico serving traditional Mexican cuisine like mole enchiladas and chiles en nogada in a stunning tiled setting (budget ~350–500 MXN per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for the airport transfer. Use Uber for a safer and metered ride from the airport. Currency exchange is best done at a bank or ATM (avoid airport exchange kiosks for better rates).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor, the ancient Aztec ceremonial site located just steps from the Zócalo. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and the excellent on-site museum which houses thousands of artifacts from the Mexica civilization. Entry is approximately 90 MXN.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (a short walk or metro ride away) to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and rotating exhibitions inside. Afterward, walk through Alameda Central park, Mexico City's oldest public park, perfect for people-watching and a midday stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bohemian neighborhood of Barrio Chino (Chinatown) near Centro or walk to the artisan markets near Ciudadela for unique handicrafts and souvenirs. End the evening with a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at El Cardinal, a classic Mexico City institution near the Zócalo known for its freshly baked bread, tamales, and café de olla (budget ~150–250 MXN).
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near Alameda Central — try tortas, esquites (corn cups), or quesadillas from a trusted street vendor or a casual local fonda (budget ~100–150 MXN).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Los Girasoles, a well-regarded restaurant near Bellas Artes offering refined Mexican cuisine with pre-Hispanic inspired dishes in a comfortable, mid-range setting (budget ~400–600 MXN per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Templo Mayor and Palacio de Bellas Artes are within easy walking distance of your hotel. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll be on cobblestones most of the day. Tuesday is a free entry day at some national museums.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — one of the most important archaeological sites in the world. Take an early bus from Terminal del Norte (reachable by metro from Centro) for a 1-hour ride. Spend the morning climbing the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon and walking the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Rest briefly at the hotel, then head to the neighborhood of Coyoacán via metro or Uber. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online as they sell out quickly. Wander through Coyoacán's charming colonial streets and central square.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere in Coyoacán's Jardín Hidalgo. Browse the artisan market stalls, listen to street musicians, and soak in the local neighborhood vibe before heading back to Centro.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel or grab tamales and atole from a street cart near the metro before heading to Teotihuacán (budget ~80–120 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near Teotihuacán — try the local specialty of pulque (fermented agave drink) and barbacoa tacos at one of the traditional eateries near the site entrance (budget ~200–300 MXN).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Coyoacán at El Jardín del Pulpo or a local taquería on the plaza — try enfrijoladas, sopes, or enchiladas verdes (budget ~250–400 MXN per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Wear sunscreen and bring water for Teotihuacán — it's an open-air site with significant sun exposure. The metro is the most efficient and budget-friendly way to get to Coyoacán.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest anthropology museums in the world. Plan to spend 2–3 hours exploring its vast collection of pre-Columbian artifacts, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. The museum is located inside Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's massive urban forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec and optionally visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec), which offers panoramic views of the city and houses the Museo Nacional de Historia. Afterward, walk or take a short Uber to the upscale Polanco neighborhood for window shopping and people-watching on Presidente Masaryk Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a cultural evening — check local listings for a performance at Palacio de Bellas Artes (ballet folklórico or classical music) or visit a nearby cantina for a traditional Mexican cantina experience with free botanas (snacks served with drinks).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Centro Histórico — try chilaquiles rojos or verdes with eggs, a quintessential Mexican morning dish (budget ~150–200 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Polanco at a mid-range restaurant — explore the area's diverse dining scene with options ranging from modern Mexican to international cuisine (budget ~350–500 MXN per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional cantina in Centro Histórico such as La Opera Bar, a historic cantina dating to 1876 with stunning Belle Époque interiors and classic Mexican dishes (budget ~300–450 MXN per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is closed on Mondays. Chapultepec is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Polanco is one of Mexico City's safest and most walkable upscale neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final morning exploring the Mercado de La Merced or Mercado de Jamaica — two of the city's most vibrant and authentic local markets. La Merced is one of the largest markets in Latin America, offering everything from fresh produce to spices, street food, and household goods. A true immersion into everyday Mexico City life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo del Estanquillo (free entry) near the Zócalo, dedicated to Mexican popular culture and the collection of writer Carlos Monsiváis. Afterward, do any last-minute souvenir shopping along Calle Moneda or at artisan shops near the Zócalo. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Centro Histórico to celebrate the trip. Optionally take a final evening walk around the illuminated Zócalo and Catedral Metropolitana, which are particularly beautiful after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the market — try fresh-squeezed juice, pan dulce (sweet bread), and a bowl of pozole or menudo from a market stall for an authentic local experience (budget ~100–150 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a comida corrida (set lunch menu) restaurant near Centro — these offer a multi-course meal including soup, main dish, drink, and dessert at excellent value (budget ~120–180 MXN).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Azul Histórico, a beloved restaurant in a beautiful courtyard setting in Centro Histórico, specializing in regional Mexican cuisine with dishes from across the country (budget ~450–650 MXN per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan airport transfer accordingly — allow at least 3 hours before international flights from AICM (Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez). Keep some MXN cash for tips, market purchases, and transport. Consider purchasing artisan goods like Talavera ceramics, embroidered textiles, or local mezcal as souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via luxury sedan service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel and freshen up. Take a leisurely private guided walking tour of the immediate Centro Histórico neighborhood: stroll through the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the façade of the Palacio Nacional, and explore the ornate Catedral Metropolitana at your own pace with an expert local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop bar overlooking the Zócalo — try Terraza del Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for panoramic views and expertly crafted mezcal cocktails. Follow with a refined dinner celebrating classic Mexican haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or post-arrival snack at hotel welcome amenity)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant or nearby Café de Tacuba — a historic 1912 institution serving traditional Mexican dishes like enchiladas and tamales in an elegant colonial setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico — a celebrated restaurant set in a stunning courtyard in Centro Histórico, renowned for regional Mexican cuisine with premium ingredients and an exceptional mezcal and tequila list

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Allow time to acclimate to Mexico City's altitude (2,240m). Keep the afternoon light given travel fatigue. Confirm hotel concierge for next-day reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Palacio Nacional with priority access — marvel at Diego Rivera's sweeping murals depicting Mexican history. Follow with a visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum, exploring the Aztec ceremonial center at the heart of the ancient city of Tenochtitlán.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided visit to the Museo del Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and rotating fine art exhibitions, including works by Rufino Tamayo and David Alfaro Siqueiros. Afterward, explore the charming streets of the nearby Alameda Central park area and browse curated artisan boutiques for premium Mexican crafts and design.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner mezcal tasting experience at a renowned mezcalería in Centro Histórico — learn about the distillation traditions of Oaxacan and Guerrero mezcal from a certified sommelier. Conclude the evening with a lavish dinner at one of the city's most prestigious fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — freshly made chilaquiles, fresh tropical fruit, artisanal pan dulce, and premium Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal, a legendary institution in Centro Histórico celebrated for its exquisite traditional Mexican cuisine, including handmade tortillas, mole, and seasonal specialties
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol (Polanco, short taxi/ride away) — Chef Enrique Olvera's globally acclaimed restaurant, consistently ranked among the world's best. The tasting menu showcases evolved Mexican flavors with extraordinary technique. Reservation essential weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in Latin America. Private guide recommended for Palacio Nacional murals for full historical context. Comfortable walking shoes advised.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Teotihuacán — depart early by luxury vehicle to beat the crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon along the Avenue of the Dead with an expert archaeologist guide providing in-depth historical narrative. Explore the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl and the colorful murals of Tetitla.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and check in to the hotel for a brief rest. Visit the stunning Museo Franz Mayer in Centro Histórico — housed in a 16th-century hospital, it holds one of Mexico's finest collections of applied arts, textiles, ceramics, and furniture. Explore the beautiful cloister garden over a light coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class performance at the Palacio de Bellas Artes — check the schedule for ballet folklórico, opera, or orchestral concerts (the Ballet Folklórico de México is a must-see cultural experience). Dress code is smart elegant. Follow with a late dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh juices, pastries, and coffee to go, or a quick sit-down with eggs and fruit
meals.lunch: Traditional barbacoa and consommé lunch at a renowned local spot near Teotihuacán — the area is famous for slow-cooked lamb barbacoa wrapped in maguey leaves, a deeply authentic regional experience
meals.dinner: Post-performance dinner at Limosneros — a sophisticated restaurant in Centro Histórico offering creative contemporary Mexican cuisine rooted in pre-Hispanic ingredients, with an outstanding natural wine and mezcal program

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán no later than 8:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds. Wear sunscreen and bring water — the site is exposed and expansive. Confirm Bellas Artes performance schedule and purchase premium tickets through hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private immersive culinary experience — join a renowned local chef for a guided morning market tour of Mercado de San Juan (Mercado Internacional), one of the city's most prestigious specialty food markets. Discover exotic ingredients, imported cheeses, fresh seafood, and artisanal products. Follow with a hands-on private cooking class learning to prepare mole negro, tamales, and a traditional dessert in a luxury kitchen studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bohemian and culturally rich neighborhood of Coyoacán via private car — visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum) with skip-the-line access for a deeply moving look into the life and art of Mexico's most celebrated painter. Stroll through Coyoacán's cobblestone streets, vibrant jardín central, and artisan market.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a private after-hours guided visit to a historic colonial mansion or cultural space. Conclude with a celebratory dinner at one of Mexico City's most elegant dining rooms.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — huevos rancheros with house-made salsa, fresh-squeezed juices, and specialty single-origin Mexican coffee from Veracruz or Chiapas
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as your lunch — a multi-course meal prepared with your chef instructor, paired with aguas frescas and artisanal mezcal
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil — Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant in Polanco, featuring a seasonal tasting menu that champions native Mexican ingredients and biodiversity. One of the top restaurants in Latin America.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Frida Kahlo Museum well in advance — timed entry tickets sell out quickly. The cooking class should be arranged through a premium culinary tourism operator for a fully personalized experience. Quintonil reservation required well ahead of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy an extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a reflective solo stroll through the Centro Histórico streets, revisiting favorite spots, browsing premium design shops on Calle Madero, and picking up artisanal souvenirs: handcrafted silver jewelry, Talavera ceramics, or fine mezcal bottles from a curated spirits boutique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) — housed in a magnificent neoclassical palace, it holds an extraordinary collection of Mexican art spanning four centuries, from the colonial era to the 20th century. Enjoy a relaxed private guided tour followed by coffee in the museum's elegant café. Optional: visit the nearby Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles), a breathtaking 18th-century palace covered in Talavera tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner — a luxurious, unhurried multi-course experience celebrating the full breadth of Mexican gastronomy and the memories of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — a full spread of Mexican breakfast classics: molletes, fresh tropical fruit platters, tamales, and artisanal hot chocolate made with Oaxacan cacao
meals.lunch: Lunch at Contramar (Colonia Roma, short ride away) — a beloved Mexico City institution famous for its impeccably fresh seafood, particularly the iconic tuna tostadas and grilled fish al pastor. A quintessential CDMX experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dulce Patria in Polanco — Chef Martha Ortiz's theatrical and visually stunning restaurant offering a poetic interpretation of Mexican cuisine, celebrated for its artistic plating, bold flavors, and deep cultural storytelling. An unforgettable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with hotel concierge — arrange private transfer to airport if departing that evening or the following morning. Purchase any remaining artisanal gifts or spirits before dinner. Tipping culture in Mexico: 15–20% is standard at fine dining establishments.
